exposure: Social factors (education level, employment status, presence of parent at admission)
Medical factors (type of anesthesia, delay of transfer from emergency, provision of operation supplies)
outcome: Decision-to-incision interval in emergency caesarean section
cohort: Women who underwent an emergency caesarean section in four hospitals in Yaoundé between January and May 2017.
finding: Several social and medical factors were associated with a longer decision-to-incision interval (>30 minutes) for emergency caesarean section.
